title: Union Berlin faces Bayern in decisive 4th round clash
seoTitle: Union Berlin faces Bayern in decisive 4th round match
subtitle: Swiss coach aims to surprise record champions while Kompany praises leadership change
excerpt: Mauro Lustrinelli arrives at Union Berlin with an offensive plan to face Bayern in the 4th Bundesliga round, while the German club's coach highlights the new.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
Union Berlin is preparing to face Bayern Munich in the 4th round of the Bundesliga, a match that has attracted great attention from fans. The confrontation will take place on Friday night, at 8:30 PM, at the Allianz Arena, and represents the first major test for the club's new Swiss coach.

What motivates Lustrinelli in the duel against Bayern

For 50-year-old Mauro Lustrinelli, the challenge is a "geile Challenge" – an opportunity to measure his team against a club with the ambition of winning the Champions League. He states that there is no fear and that the goal is to apply a clear and convicted plan, regardless of the formations Bayern might adopt.

How Union intends to change its tactical identity

Lustrinelli points out that Union Berlin will adopt a more offensive and ball-playing style, different from the traditional "Union-DNA" based on defensive transition promoted by Urs Fischer. The Swiss coach emphasizes that the formation – whether in a back four, three, or five – is secondary to the goal of causing trouble for Bayern and preventing the opponent from imposing their rhythm.

Vincent Kompany's reaction to Union's new leadership

Vincent Kompany, Bayern's coach, acknowledges the major impact of Lustrinelli's arrival. He comments that Union underwent a "grande Umbruch" (major upheaval) and that the new coach arrived with clear ideas, having won the Swiss title before taking over the German club.

Bayern's tactical preparation for the match

According to Lustrinelli, Bayern usually varies its game plan, alternating between different systems, such as a 4-4-2 or a back five. Union has been training to respond to these variations, aiming to be ready for any change the opponent implements.

Next steps for Union after the duel

If Union fails to achieve positive results in Munich, the team will still have an international break before facing newly promoted Elversberg on October 10th, a match that could be decisive in securing the first win of the season. Lustrinelli reinforces that "results are the bread we need" and that the project is just beginning.

With information from Blick.
